title: On release day an existing customer keeps its one representative
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have an active staff member at the test location with the "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A.
  • Use customer A, which had sales rep A as its sales representative before the release was installed.
  • Use customer B, which had no sales representative before the release was installed.
  • Use customer C, whose representative was no longer a user of the shop before the release was installed.
  • Have notes of how the three customer pages looked before the release was installed.
  • Open the design pictures "customer-00-b-customer-page.png" (board 2.0), "customer-01-b-customer-dialog-open.png" (board 2.1) and "customer-02-b-new.png" (board 2.2) attached to this case beside the browser window at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • With the release installed, open customer A's page in a desktop browser at least 1024 pixels wide.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Read customer A's page.
  2. Open Edit Customer for customer A.
  3. Open customer B's page.
  4. Open customer C's page.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • "Sales Representative" reads sales rep A.
  • The page reads as before.

Step 2:

  • One "Sales Representative" field reads sales rep A.
  • There is no Service Parts or Part Sales field.

Step 3:

  • "Sales Representative" reads "Unassigned" where it used to read "N/A".

Step 4:

  • "Sales Representative" reads "Unassigned".
  • This is one of the few customers whose representative was no longer a user of the shop.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11268 (Story 4, Give a customer default representatives)

  • S4-E1: “On release day every existing customer has the one "Sales Representative" field, with no Service Parts or Part Sales field, and keeps its one representative, so the customer page and every invoice read exactly as before, except that an empty field reads "Unassigned" instead of "N/A". About 10 customers whose representative is no longer a user of the shop are the exception: they read "Unassigned".”
  • S4-R19: “The customer page shows the representatives with the window's labels, in the window's order: "Sales Representative" or "Sales Representative - Service Labor", then "Sales Representative - Service Parts" when added, then "Sales Representative - Part Sales" when added. An empty one reads "Unassigned". The Sales Representative rows show on every customer, whether or not the customer has an address. The other fields on the page keep today's rule of showing only when the customer has an address.”
  • Release day: “Every existing customer keeps its one sales representative and is not split, so the customer page reads as before (S4-E1). The exception is about 10 customers whose representative is no longer a user of the shop: they read "Unassigned". One wording changes: a customer with no representative reads "Unassigned" instead of "N/A" (S4-R19).”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 19: “19. (a) Yes, add the exception.”
